text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Interior Minister Driss Basri tells French businessmen that aim of talks between government and unions is to achieve lasting social peace.
- German Democrat Socialist Party SPD party hails Morocco's democratic process.
- Arab justice ministers meeting in Rabat voice respect for King Hassan's stand over Arab issues.
- Approval of budget law for 1997 raises question of whether streamlining expenses will trigger economic pickup.
- James Baker, U.N. special envoy in Western Sahara, expected to return to the region next month.
- Arab Maghreb Union secretariat based in Rabat to trim two thirds of staff starting May 15.
- Telecommunications utility Office National des Postes et Telecommunications (ONPT) raises cost of domestic calls.
- Cuts in expenditures included in next year's budget will delay implementation of social benefits.
